interpretation: Every native total difference is attributed to explicit component deltas, allowing rounded external sums. Attribution is not proof that either complete total is correct.

findings.evidence: Native absolute longitude subtraction can exceed 180 degrees; its built-in circular alternative is reported separately.
Native midpoint is linear and final angle unwrapped. Separate circular-formula output retains external historical mean-motion inputs.
Our 12 daytime/12 nighttime temporal hours differ from external elapsed civil-hour arithmetic.

External declination_of_planets tests north/south before normalizing sidereal longitude plus ayanamsa; values >=360 receive the wrong hemisphere. Its inverse-Lagrange interpolation also differs from our six piecewise linear segments. Neither is modern physical declination.
Our eligible pairs require <1 degree; native closest-pair routine has no 1-degree cutoff and can discard all wars if a luminary is closest.
Native Sun-Moon absolute subtraction is unwrapped. Actual range violations and signed classifications are not silently corrected.
Degree-zone, varga and rounding policies are visible term by term; no aggregate match is asserted.
